{{nihongo|'''Hokotsuki Shrine'''|桙衝神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

'''Hokotsuki Shrine''' (ほこつきじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Hokotsuki, {{ill|Sukagawa, Fukushima|ar|سوكاغاوا (فوكوشيما)|azb|سوکاقاوا، فوکوشیما|ce|Сукагава|ceb|Sukagawa (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Sukagawa|de|Sukagawa|eo|Sukagawa|es|Sukagawa|fa|سوکاگاوا، فوکوشیما|fi|Sukagawa|fr|Sukagawa|gl|Sukagawa|id|Sukagawa, Fukushima|it|Sukagawa|ja|須賀川市|ko|스카가와시|mg|Sukagawa|mzn|سوکاگاوا، فوکوشیما|nl|Sukagawa|pl|Sukagawa|pt|Sukagawa|ro|Sukagawa|ru|Сукагава|sr|Сукагава|sv|Sukagawa|tg|Сукагава|tl|Sukagawa, Fukushima|tr|Sukagawa|tt|Сукагава|uk|Сукаґава|ur|سوکاکاوا، فوکوشیما|uz|Sukagava (Fukushima)|vi|Sukagawa, Fukushima|war|Sukagawa, Fukushima|zh|須賀川市|zh_classical|須賀川市|zh_min_nan|Sukagawa-chhī|zh_yue|須賀川|qid=Q819664}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}. === History ===
According to tradition, when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru no Mikoto}} was on his eastern campaign, he climbed Mount Kameiyama (Kamuiyama) and prayed for victory to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Kami}}, using a large stone on the mountaintop as an altar. === Festivals ===
* Taiko Shishi (Drum Lion Dance) – Held once every three years (in leap years of the old lunar calendar) in October: an evening festival on the first Saturday, followed by the main festival on Sunday. Local men from the Hokotsuki area apply makeup, wear costumes, and dance while beating drums. It was designated an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Sukagawa City on April 1, 1968 ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 43).<ref>[http://www.city.sukagawa.fukushima.jp/2982.htm List of Designated Cultural Properties of Sukagawa City] – Sukagawa City, accessed November 12, 2018.</ref>

=== Cultural Properties ===
=== Cultural Properties Designated by Fukushima Prefecture ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties
** Hokotsuki Shrine Main Hall (with 12 ridge tags) (Structure) – Designated May 4, 1976 (Shōwa 51).

=== Cultural Properties Designated by Sukagawa City ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties
** Hokotsuki Shrine Worship Hall (Structure) – Designated April 1, 1971 (Shōwa 46).
** Hokotsuki Shrine Zuishin Gate (Structure) – Designated April 1, 1971 (Shōwa 46).
** Hokotsuki Shrine Kagura Hall (Structure) – Designated April 1, 1971 (Shōwa 46).
** Hokotsuki Shrine Ema-Tsunagi Koma (Painting) – Stored at the Sukagawa City Museum of History and Folklore. Designated April 1, 1981 (Shōwa 86).
** Artifacts Excavated from the Hokotsuki Shrine Ritual Site (Archaeological Materials) – Designated March 26, 2001 (Heisei 13).
* Intangible Folk Cultural Properties
** Hokotsuki Shrine Taiko Shishi – Designated April 1, 1968 (Shōwa 43).
* Historic Sites
** Hokotsuki Shrine Ritual Site – Designated March 17, 1998 (Heisei 10).
